title: Pretty huge disappointment
text:
Pretty huge disappointment. I was pretty excited when I putting this vacuum together and reading the manual but... I’ve vacuumed my house once and was just more and more disappointed. I do want to say that I am the type of person that vacuums at least six days a week (sometimes twice a day, because toddlers) and I also detail with the vacuum at least every other day. I need a vacuum that does the job and does it efficiently. Maybe if you’re one of those people I’ve read about that vacuums once a week this would be ok for you. If you actually want a detailed clean, keep searching.

So let’s start with the good points:
I do like the idea of being able to take apart all of parts and wash them. And the idea of having a washable filter is great. It does work well on the floors, we have mostly wood and a few shorter pile rugs. The cord rewind is also a great feature (in theory) but I find that having to yank 25’ of cord out to be a little annoying already. The dusting accessory is nice and works well for house plants and shelves. And that’s it for the good parts... like I said, pretty huge disappointment.

Now the not so great parts (and there’s a lot of them, so buckle up and grab a snack):
The washable filter was originally what sold me on this particular vacuum but now that I’ve used it once (see pictures) I know I’m going to have to wash the filters at least once a week because hair and a ton of dirt gets directly to the filter. Which means ordering extra filters because they have to air dry and as I said before, I pretty much vacuum daily. I know understand WHY the whole vacuum needs to come apart for cleaning, hair gets stuck and wrapped around all over the ‘cyclone’ parts of the dirt cup. This vacuum doesn’t have a light! That’s my own fault for assuming it did, but I honestly didn’t know that modern vacuums didn’t just all have them. I find it incredibly annoying that I now have to switch on all the lights in every room to make sure I don’t miss anything. Even my super cheap stick vacuum has a light *facepalm*. Now let’s talk about these accessories... man o man what a HUGE letdown. Let’s start with this huge joke of an “extension” hose. It’s a foot long. That’s not much of an ‘extension’ in my book. I don’t know what kind of giant they have in the pictures but I’m 5’3” and I am now going to have to haul around a step stool to reach pretty much everything above my head. Using the crevice tool gives you another foot but you can’t use the other accessories on the end of it. And speaking of the crevice tool, if you’re using the extension hose there’s no where to put it so you have to carry it around while you use the other tools. The corner tool is the most awkward thing I have ever used and you have to stoop down into an awkward angle to use it. It’s just a weird design and not very user friendly at all. The ‘turbo pet eraser’ is another total letdown. Even the pressure from its own suction is enough to stop it completely. You have to have a very light touch while using it which means it’s actually pretty useless for getting the dog hair off the couch. It doesn’t work at all for pillows and couch covers because the fabric lifts up slightly and that’s enough to stop the brush head. Being that their whole advertisement scheme is based around being a pet friendly vacuum I’m left feeling pretty confused about that. The swivel feature is ok but kind of awkward to get used to and the roller can only fit about two inches under the furniture.

Overall, huge disappointment. I don’t know who they use for product testers that told them this thing was ready to go to market but they need to hire some people who have actually used a vacuum before; this thing is a disaster. I’m not sure if I’m going to go through the hassle of cleaning this thing to return it yet, but I’ll update if I do.
